messages:
kevin: heads-up — we need a bursty GPU capacity lane in eu-west4 for a new customer PoC. They want low-latency web inference but only for spikes. wondering about node size and preemptible tradeoffs.
anita: +1. are we thinking 1x-a10g per node or denser like 4x-a100? cost vs cold-starts will differ a lot.
mike: for bursty spiky traffic i'd lean 1 GPU per node (a10g) so autoscaler can scale granularly. 4x-a100 reduces cost/TOP but increases bin-packing and startup time.
kevin: agreed. customer tolerates slight variance in accuracy so a10g quantized model should work. also want to keep min nodes at 0 so we don't waste reserved capacity.
lia: note: EU quota for a10g in eu-west4 is currently 24 GPUs -> we'd need quota increase to support worst-case burst. i filed a support ticket (GCP) earlier but no response yet. ticket: 1234567890.
kevin: thanks. can someone run a quick cost calc for 0->20 nodes with preemptible vs committed? rough estimate is fine.
mike: rough numbers: preemptible a10g ~ $0.20/hr, standard ~$0.80/hr. so 20 preemptible nodes ~= $96/day, standard ~= $384/day. but preemptible evictions add retry overhead and potential tail-latency.
anita: if we set autoscaler profile to optimize for latency and use smaller nodes we can keep cold-start p95 < 700ms for warmed containers. but the first pod startup will still be ~20–40s on node provisioning. consider a small keep-warm pool (1-2 nodes) with a taint for best-effort.
kevin: ok plan: create node pool 'burst-a10g-ephemeral' with min=0 max=20, autoscaler 0.5 utilization target, preemptible nodes by default, and run 2 keep-warm nodes in a separate pool 'gpu-warm-small' (n=2, a10g non-preemptible) with taint 'redwood/gpu:reserved:NoSchedule'. pods that can tolerate best-effort get scheduled on preemptible.
lia: config suggestion (gcloud):
```
gcloud container node-pools create burst-a10g-ephemeral \
  --cluster=redwood-eu-west4-main \
  --machine-type=n2-standard-16 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a10g,count=1 \
  --preemptible \
  --num-nodes=0 \
  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=20 \
  --labels=pool=burst-a10g,env=prod \
  --metadata=disable-legacy-endpoints=true
```
lia: also make sure GPU driver DaemonSet is in nodepool's taint/label scope and gpu-feature-discovery is enabled.
kevin: what about node autoscaler balancing across AZs? we should set spread by zones and use max-surge for quick scale.
mike: cluster-autoscaler flags: `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` and use taint-based evictions. set `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 5m for burst pools so we drop idle quick.
anita: ops concern: preemptible eviction during a high-concurrency test could cause cascading retries — suggest circuit-breaker at application layer and fallback to CPU-only cheap model hosted in dedicated pool.
kevin: agreed. add a fallback route in smart routing for eu region to CPU pool. can product/infra own the routing config?
lia: i'll draft a terraform module for the two pools and a quota sanity check step that fails if quota < requested. also will add an automated ticket comment to GCP quota request.
sre-bot: deploy-checklist: remember to add nodePool annotation `redwood.com/allow-spot=true` and update cost-center tag.
kevin: action items: lia to open terraform PR + quota preflight, anita to validate cold-start perf with a10g image (dev env), mike to run cost/eviction sims. i'll chase the quota ticket if GCP doesn't respond in 24h.
anita: noted, starting perf run now. will paste results here. :thumbsup:
mike: i'll put a small k6 script and run 3 scenarios (steady, spike, spike+eviction) and share numbers.
kevin: thanks team — keep updates in this thread. we'll target a soft launch to the PoC by end of next week.
